U.S. Census first-name and surname frequencies.

Source: R/data.R
census.names.Rd

Names with how often each is a given name (by gender) and a surname in U.S. Census Bureau name lists. Used to decide name order and to score gender.

Usage

census.names

Format

A data.table::data.table with 195,311 rows and 5 variables, keyed on name:

name

upper-case name (a factor)

male_value

people with this first name recorded male (2020)

female_value

people with this first name recorded female (2020)

first_name_value

count as a first name: male_value + female_value

last_name_value

people with this surname (2020)

Source

U.S. Census Bureau, Frequently Occurring First Names and Last Names from the 2020 Census: https://www.census.gov/topics/population/genealogy/data/2020_names.html

Details

Built by data-raw/census_names.R from the Census Bureau's 2020 release, "Frequently Occurring First Names and Last Names from the 2020 Census" (revised 2026-04-09): 53,615 first names held by 91 or more people, with counts by sex, and 156,621 surnames held by 92 or more people, each list ending in an ALL OTHER NAMES row. The script downloads the files, records their hashes in data-raw/census-names-src.csv, and rebuilds the table, so it can be refreshed when the Bureau publishes new lists.

Until November 2026 the package shipped a table from the 1990 first-name lists (1,219 male and 4,275 female names, given as percentages and scaled to counts) and the 2010 surname file. The 2020 lists cover ten times as many given names and fit Form 990 names better (see NEWS.md). See vignette("gender-scoring").
